newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ABB SAYS TO HAVE 1 SHARE LISTING LONGTERM.
newsitem.headline: ABB SAYS TO HAVE 1 SHARE LISTING LONGTERM.

text.p: International engineer ABB said on Friday that it would have one share listing in the longterm and that its staff costs would fall this year and coming year.
Currently, ABB's two parent companies' shares are traded in Zurich and Stockholm.
ABB's chief executive Goran Lindahl stressed, however, that the issue was not a priority and that some tax effects remained to be solved.
"It's not an urgent issue but sooner or later we will get there (to one share)," Lindahl told an analyst meeting.
Also, Lindahl said staff costs would fall after remaining largely unchanged in the first half of the year.
"I estimate that staff costs will fall to the end of the year and then keep doing so, by a few percentage points, in coming years," Lindahl said.
At the end of June this year, ABB had 216,124 employees against 214,894 at the start of 1997.
ABB reported a two percent rise in six-month net profit to $567 million which was below a market forecast of 4.5 percent.
